chunks.rationale: test/sidebar.test.tsx describe 'Sidebar snooze nested submenu (#583)'. New cases sit after the existing drill-in / ArrowUp-Down tests: click-open focuses first menuitem, keyboard-focused … then click does the same, ArrowDown works with no extra focus(), Escape / outside click / Fork restore …, Rename keeps the title input, switching cards does not bounce. pressFocused, not press(el). Identity is assert.ok(a === b); assert.equal on nodes hangs on circular fibers.
risks: The two-card bounce test depends on menu-src rendering earlier in the tree than menu-noise (p1 then p2). A later sidebar reorder would make the naive restore look green and hide the steal.
keyboard-on-… uses click after more.focus(), not Enter/Space. jsdom does not synthesize a button click from Enter, so a real keydown-on-trigger hole would not be caught.

chunks.rationale: ThreadCard focus layout effect in src/components/Sidebar.tsx. On the false→true edge of snoozeMenuOpen, focusMenuEdge(menu, 'first') so arrows hit the menu's onKeyDown without Tab. pendingMenuFocus still wins for drill-in (preset) and back (snooze) so ArrowRight/Left do not get overwritten. On close, moreBtnRef.focus() unless renamingRef is set. Restore is skipped when activeElement is already a live node that is not this trigger — opening card B closes A, and A's later-in-tree effect must not yank focus off B's first item.
risks: justOpened is a ref, not a render bit, so a 700ms thread patch while the menu is open cannot re-steal focus. Clearing menuWasOpen anywhere else would re-trigger first-item focus on the next panel toggle.

Outside-click restore runs even when the click target is the search field. In the real app that target may already have been focused by mousedown; we steal it back. That matches the requested contract but is unlike native <select>.

chunks.rationale: moreBtnRef on [data-more-btn]. No change to click contract, nested keys, data-snooze-preset / data-snooze-clear, or #582 stacking (data-menu-open, .group:has([data-snooze-menu]) z-index 8). first enabled item is usually [data-snooze-item]; without onSetSnoozed it is Fork.
risks: Tab still walks every native menuitem. This is open-focus, not a tabindex=-1 roving set.
ArrowDown on the closed … trigger still does nothing — the menu is not mounted, so its onKeyDown is not listening. Enter/Space/click are the only openers.
This branch still carries the #583 nested markup plus ArrowUp/Down from the parent worktree. Reviewers landing stacked PRs will conflict on Sidebar.tsx.
data-snooze-preset / data-snooze-clear and #582 stacking were not edited this turn.
